question: Is E62 the one-time legacy amnesty or a recurring update bypass, and does the update bypass reach this plugin's private muse serve host?

isolation.privateConfig: private-config (settings.json plus trust.json; no owner config read or written)
isolation.trustPrecondition: trust.json for ws-a was seeded in store-a and later in private-config; this is a precondition, not a measurement

plugin.name: e65-probe
plugin.hook: SessionStart `mark`; command node hooks/mark-a.mjs, changed to hooks/mark-b.mjs, then hooks/mark-c.mjs

A.setup: settings.json seeded with BOTH E62 amnesty records before the fresh project-scope install

install.warning: third-party plugin: hooks require review before activation

A.reading: With both amnesty records seeded before the fresh install, the update reported `modified`, the changed hook did not run, and the stored trusted hash and flags were unchanged. The flag pair suppresses the migration on 1.4.25.

B.control: E62 (docs/evidence/2026-11-26-r31-e62.json): flag absent at fresh install, changed hook ran and the amnesty pair was written
B.why: The Arm A setup differs only by the seeded flag pair, so E62 is the valid flag-absent control.

C.setup: Private XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the shape writeMuseHostConfig() writes (schema_version, run, the six reminder rows, context, compaction), XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at store-a/data; no e65 approval entry
deviations: run.system_prompt was removed because the echo provider exits 1 with `provider does not support base instructions` (run-c-1).
run.toolset was removed because with no MCP server registered the host exits 1 with `unknown tool mcp__opencode__*` (run-c-2).
trust.json was added after `muse plugins update` refused with `project-local plugin source is blocked because the workspace is untrusted` (update-c); this is the same trust precondition Arm A used.
These removals keep the property under test: a private config with no user approval row.

beforeApproval.reading: The user-approved hook in store-a did not run in the private host; the plugin record is visible (`trust=project-trusted`) but the approval is not.

updateInPrivateConfig.firstAttemptError: invalid-plugin-package: project-local plugin source is blocked because the workspace is untrusted

C.reading: Once an approval exists inside the private config, `muse plugins update` plus one turn ran the changed hook (marker C) with no new approval and wrote the full amnesty pair into that config. The mechanism therefore reaches a private muse serve config; it does not reach the user's approval, which the private config never carries.

productionShape.spawn: muse serve --trust-workspace with a per-process XDG_CONFIG_HOME from writeMuseHostConfig()
productionShape.privateConfigLifetime: mkdtemp per host process; settings.json is rewritten each start
productionShape.approvalSource: the private settings file only; the user's real settings.json is not copied
productionShape.updateCaller: the plugin never runs `muse plugins update` or `muse plugins approve`
productionShape.reading: The measured bypass needs an approval inside the private config and an update issued against it. The plugin creates neither, so a normal session has no live bypass path; the reachable finding is the user-approved hook being inert in the private host, not a changed hook running.

markers.markerB: not fired (Arm A second turn); fired only after an explicit approval in the private config

result: H3 with a scope condition. Arm A shows the seeded flag pair suppresses the one-time amnesty, so E62 was the legacy migration, not a recurring bypass. Arm C shows the private host does not inherit the user's approval (no marker, review_needed), but a private config that holds its own approval runs an updated hook without re-approval and writes the amnesty pair. The bypass reaches the private config shape, not the normal production session, because the plugin never approves or updates inside that config.
branch: D254 H3: stop the run; P1/P2 become an owner decision (block plugin origins or accept the inert production path)
limits: Echo provider only; no paid model turn.

The private config omitted system_prompt and toolset because the echo provider rejects them; the approval-isolation property is preserved but the config is not byte-identical to writeMuseHostConfig().
The private-config update needed a seeded trust.json; that is a precondition, not a measurement.
Arm C reused store-a/data, so its update rewrote the shared plugin cache after Arm A's recorded state.
`hook/list` was not called; the SDK type carries no trust status, so it would not have distinguished the states.
